brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.evidence: drawer:0#0,0#cut on the cut (south) face of the half-north base piece:0,0,0;half-n; house rules capOpenFaces and lockJoints applied, check_build clear.

Every spike junction that includes the drawer cell 0,0 was refused. With bases present (south junction 0,0/1,0/0,1, south-west 0,0/0,1/-1,1, north-east 0,0/1,-1/1,0) each returned SPIKE_CLASH, and the configurator's suggested alternative was always a spike at a junction one cell away that does not include 0,0. With the neighbouring bases removed the same junction returned TOO_FEW_CELLS. So no spike can stand at any corner of the drawer cell while its drawer is there.

requirements.requirement: Drawer and spike at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: Because no spike can be placed at any corner of cell 0,0 alongside its drawer (see above), the same-corner touching arrangement is not achievable. The drawer alone is built at 0,0 as the closest feasible part of the brief.

finish.summary: Built the drawer at cell 0,0 (half-north base with a drawer on its cut face), but the spike at the same corner proved impossible: a spike placed at any three-base junction that includes the drawer cell was refused with SPIKE_CLASH every time, the configurator instead offering only junctions one cell away that exclude the drawer cell; without those bases the junction returns TOO_FEW_CELLS. The drawer therefore stands alone, capped and joint-locked, and the spike/same-corner requirement is reported unmet rather than substituted with a spike at a different corner.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: One drawer + one spike at the same corner — I'll survey the build and socket options for a layout where they touch.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
Ask again with a family or a few words (text) to see the parts themselves.
